text: On it. `Interval.fromISO` calls `DateTime.fromISO`/`Duration.fromISO` on each side before it does its own validity check, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` the inner `InvalidDateTimeError` escapes instead of the method's own `InvalidIntervalError` ("unparsable"). A subagent is fixing that in src/interval.js and verifying the full jest suite; ETA ~8 min.

Got it. Likely a year-100 boundary heuristic in src/impl/util.js (2-digit-year / century handling) that corrupts month arithmetic crossing February. A second subagent is reproducing it and fixing the root cause; ETA ~12 min. Bug #1 is still in progress.
Status: the fix in src/interval.js is being applied and the full jest suite is being re-run to confirm nothing regressed. ETA ~5 min.
Status: still in progress. The year-100/February boundary bug in src/impl/util.js is being reproduced and fixed, then the whole jest suite is re-run. ETA ~10 min.

Got it. `isInDST()` in src/datetime.js likely compares the current offset against an offset from a fixed month shift, which fails for years like 1974 (USA) where DST spans nearly the whole year. A subagent is reproducing and fixing it; ETA ~15 min. #1 and #2 are still in progress.

Got it. A subagent is now checking every unit pair through `Duration#normalize`/`shiftTo` against the conversion matrix in src/impl/conversions.js and fixing the root cause in src/duration.js; ETA ~15 min. #1, #2 and #4 are still in progress.

Bug #1 fixed. `Interval.fromISO` in src/interval.js now parses each side defensively (try/catch around DateTime.fromISO / Duration.fromISO), so when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true it throws `InvalidIntervalError` ("unparsable") instead of leaking the inner `InvalidDateTimeError`; with the setting off it returns an invalid Interval with reason "unparsable" exactly as before. Also fixed the "asISO 8601" typo in the explanation (no test asserts that string). Verified: full jest suite unchanged (892 passed / 2 pre-existing failures in toFormat.test.js, unrelated ICU locale output), interval suite 127/127 green.
#1 is done (see previous message): Interval.fromISO now throws InvalidIntervalError under Settings.throwOnInvalid; full jest suite unchanged (892 passed, 2 pre-existing unrelated failures).
#2 still in progress: the year-100/February boundary bug in src/impl/util.js is being reproduced and fixed, then the full jest suite is re-run. ETA ~6 min.
#4 still in progress: isInDST() in src/datetime.js is being fixed for the 1974-USA case, then the full jest suite is re-run. ETA ~10 min.
#5 still in progress: all unit pairs through Duration#normalize are being checked against the conversion matrix and the root cause fixed in src/duration.js. ETA ~12 min.

Got it. Negative (BCE) years aren't zero-padded correctly by the year-padding helper in src/impl/util.js, so `toISODate()` gives e.g. `-50-01-01` instead of `-0050-01-01`. A subagent is fixing that (coordinating with the other util.js fix so the two don't clash); ETA ~15 min. #2, #4, #5 are still in progress.

Bug #5 fixed. Root cause: the conversion tables in src/duration.js were missing entries — `casualMatrix.years.quarters`, `casualMatrix.quarters.seconds`, and `accurateMatrix.years.quarters` — so `convert()` returned undefined/NaN and `as`/`get` silently masked it as 0. Added the three entries (quarters: 4, 91*24*60*60 seconds). Verified by exhaustively checking all 81 ordered unit pairs (as / normalize().as / shiftTo().as, casual and longterm): 0 bad pairs after, 18 bad before. Jest: 892 passed / 2 pre-existing unrelated toFormat failures, identical to baseline; duration suite 114/114 green.

Bug #4 fixed. Root cause: `isInDST` compared the current offset against the offset of the *same day-of-month* in January and May; in 1974 US DST ran Jan 6 → Oct 27, so for any day ≥ 6 the January reference was itself in DST and the comparison always failed. Anchored both references to `day: 1` (src/datetime.js). Verified: 1974-01-06/06-15/10-26 in America/New_York now report true, 1974-01-05 and 1974-10-27 false, and 2018 New York / Sydney / fixed-offset cases unchanged. Jest: 892 passed / 2 pre-existing unrelated toFormat failures, identical to baseline.

Bug #7 fixed. Root cause: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js padded the string form of the number, so negative years became `0-50` instead of `-0050`. It now strips the sign, pads the magnitude and re-prefixes it, so `toISODate()` gives `-0050-01-01`, `-0001-01-01` etc. while positive years and long values are unchanged. Jest: 892 passed / 2 pre-existing unrelated toFormat failures, identical to baseline.

Got it. `FixedOffsetZone.instance(...)` currently accepts a non-numeric offset and produces a "valid" zone with a NaN offset, so a DateTime built in it isn't invalid. A subagent is fixing that in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js (making such a zone `isValid === false` while numeric offsets keep working); ETA ~15 min. #2 is still in progress.
#1 done (Interval.fromISO throws InvalidIntervalError under Settings.throwOnInvalid).
#2 still in progress: the year-100/February arithmetic bug in src/impl/util.js is being reproduced and fixed, then the full suite is re-run. ETA ~5 min.
#4 done (isInDST now correct for 1974 USA).
#5 done (missing quarters/seconds entries added to the Duration conversion matrices).
#7 done (padStart now pads negative years correctly, e.g. -0050-01-01).
#8 still in progress: FixedOffsetZone.instance with a non-numeric offset is being made invalid (zone.isValid === false, DateTime invalid), then the full suite is re-run. ETA ~13 min.

Bug #8 fixed. Root cause: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `true`, so a non-numeric offset produced a "valid" zone with a NaN offset. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed) && !Number.isNaN(this.fixed)`. Verified: `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp"|NaN|undefined|null|{})` is invalid, and DateTimes built via `fromObject({zone})`, `setZone`, `fromMillis/fromSeconds/fromJSDate/fromISO/fromFormat/fromRFC2822` with such a zone are invalid with reason "unsupported zone"; numeric offsets (0, 3, -5, 5.5, UTC+6 specifiers) unchanged. Jest: 892 passed / 2 pre-existing unrelated toFormat failures, identical to baseline; zones suite 32/32 green.
